title: The Tokenization Imperative
summary: From language encoding to AI infrastructure, modern tokenization shapes how language models represent, compress, and process information. The research examines tokenization as a foundational architectural choice influencing context utilization, computational efficiency, representation quality, and downstream model intelligence.
category: Tokenization + Modern NLP + Language Models + Representation Learning + Subword Tokenization + Context Efficiency + Compute Efficiency + Model Intelligence + Language Representation + AI Infrastructure + LLMs

title: Context Language Models
summary: Context Language Models move AI beyond static context windows toward model-owned cognitive state, enabling models to govern, adapt, retain, rewrite, compact, and optimize their own working memory. The approach treats context as an active computational resource rather than passive input, supporting adaptive context management, long-horizon reasoning, multi-agent coordination, and more compute-efficient inference.
category: Context Language Models + Model-Owned Context + Cognitive State + Working Memory + Context Management + Adaptive Context + Context Optimization + Long-Horizon Reasoning + Agent Memory + Multi-Agent Systems + Context Compression + Inference Efficiency + Compute-Efficient AI

title: Agensh: Designing the Operating Model for Autonomous AI
summary: Agensh reframes multi-agent AI from centralized orchestration to self-organizing intelligence—enabling agents to discover and claim sub-tasks, coordinate through shared context, communicate through distributed state, verify results, and merge progress asynchronously. By scaling to 1,024 agents, the approach demonstrates how shared context, decentralized coordination, distributed decision-making, and emergent specialization can form an operating model for autonomous AI organizations.
category: Agensh + Multi-Agent Systems + Self-Organizing AI + Agentic Organizations + Shared Context + Context Management + Decentralized Coordination + Distributed Decision-Making + Multi-Agent Collaboration + Emergent Specialization + Agent Orchestration + Organizational Intelligence + Agent Scaling + Autonomous AI

title: JEV-as-a-Judge: Confidence-Gated AI Evaluation
summary: JEV reframes AI evaluation from universal LLM judging to selective intelligence—routing compute, cost, and reasoning based on evaluator confidence and uncertainty. The approach enables evaluation systems to reserve deeper reasoning for ambiguous or low-confidence cases while using lighter evaluation paths where confidence is sufficient, creating a more adaptive and compute-efficient evaluation architecture.
category: JEV + AI Evaluation + Confidence-Gated Evaluation + LLM-as-a-Judge + Selective Intelligence + Adaptive Evaluation + Compute Allocation + Evaluation Efficiency + Reasoning Allocation + AI Evaluators

title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
summary: RRSI introduces a framework for recursively improving agent harnesses while controlling overfitting during self-improvement. Rather than optimizing an agent solely against its existing evaluation environment, RRSI regularizes recursive optimization to encourage improvements that transfer across tasks and conditions. The work positions the agent harness itself—not just the underlying model—as an object of continual optimization, creating a pathway toward more robust and transferable agent intelligence.
category: RRSI + Recursive Self-Improvement + Agent Harnesses + Regularized Optimization + Transferable Agent Intelligence + Agent Optimization + Self-Improving Agents + Agent Evaluation + Harness Engineering + Long-Horizon Agents

title: CORAL: An LLM-Native Harness for Production Recommender Systems
summary: CORAL introduces an LLM-native harness for production recommender systems that reframes recommendation from a static pipeline into a closed-loop decision system. The framework uses LLM-driven agents to coordinate recommendation objectives, retrieval, ranking, reasoning, execution, and feedback, enabling systems to continuously adapt based on outcomes and evolving user context. This architecture shifts recommender design toward autonomous, feedback-driven decision loops where the LLM acts as an orchestration and control layer across the recommendation lifecycle.
category: CORAL + LLM-Native Recommender Systems + Production Recommenders + Closed-Loop Decision Systems + Agentic Recommendation + LLM Agents + Feedback Loops + Recommendation Orchestration + Adaptive Decision Systems + Generative AI

title: The Control Layer
summary: The Control Layer examines the emerging need for explicit control mechanisms in agentic AI systems, arguing that reliable agents require more than strong generation capabilities—they need structured governance over execution. The work focuses on controlling agent behavior across planning, tool use, state transitions, verification, and recovery, positioning the control layer as the architectural mechanism that constrains, coordinates, and supervises agent execution. This shifts the agentic AI frontier from generating actions toward governing how those actions are selected, executed, verified, and adapted over time.
category: Control Layer + Agentic AI + Agent Governance + Execution Control + Agent Orchestration + Tool Use + State Transitions + Verification + Recovery + Reliable Agents + AI Systems Architecture

title: AutoSaddler: Turning Agent Traces into Durable System Upgrades
summary: AutoSaddler transforms agent execution traces into durable improvements to agent infrastructure by systematically diagnosing failures, generating structured patches, and validating whether proposed changes generalize beyond the original failure cases. Rather than treating traces as passive logs, the framework turns execution experience into an iterative engineering loop—identifying failure patterns, modifying system components, and evaluating whether those modifications improve future agent behavior. This reframes agent reliability as an evolving systems problem where execution traces become a source of continuous infrastructure improvement.
category: AutoSaddler + Agent Traces + Failure Diagnosis + Structured Patching + Agent Evolution + Generalization + Agent Reliability + Continuous Improvement + Self-Improving Agents + Agent Infrastructure

title: Prime Agent: The Runtime That Turns LLMs Into Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Prime Agent is an open-source runtime for long-horizon AI agents that combines persistent execution, recursive subagents, programmatic computation, retained histories, memories, and reusable skills. Its architecture separates information management from computation management, allowing agents to preserve and refine state across extended trajectories while dynamically allocating test-time compute. The runtime also introduces recovery, verification, resource accounting, and continual refinement—shifting agent design from short-lived tool execution toward persistent, self-improving execution systems.
category: Prime Agent + Long-Horizon Agents + RLM Harness + Persistent State + Recursive Orchestration + Continual Learning + Agent Runtime + Test-Time Compute + Multi-Agent Systems + Self-Improving Agents
